title: Sort each living thing into the habitat where you are most likely to find it
instructions: Drag each living thing into the habitat where you are MOST likely to find it on a typical school campus. Some species can live in more than one habitat — pick the one this chapter most associates with.

bins.name: On trees and bushes
bins.description: Birds, squirrels, insects, lichens and tree-living plants.

bins.name: On the ground / in soil
bins.description: Ants, beetles, earthworms, fallen-leaf life, soil microbes.

bins.name: On walls and stones
bins.description: Gecko lizards, spiders, mosses, lichens that cling to flat surfaces.

bins.name: In water (pond / tank)
bins.description: Pondweed, tadpoles, water-striders, small fish, algae.

bins.name: In the air
bins.description: Flying insects — butterflies, bees — and small birds in flight.

items.name: Sparrow
items.explanation: Sparrows nest and rest on trees and bushes.

items.name: Bark lichen
items.explanation: Lichens commonly cling to tree bark.

items.name: Black ant
items.explanation: Ants forage on the ground and tunnel in soil.

items.name: Beetle
items.explanation: Many beetles forage on the ground.

items.name: Wall moss
items.explanation: Moss grows on damp walls and stones.

items.name: Tadpole
items.explanation: Tadpole is the larva of a frog, in water.
